//: Plugins the marketplace sync must never bundle into apps/desktop/resources/plugins. Ids listed here are skipped by scripts/sync-bundled-plugins.mjs and any already-expanded copy is removed.
//cn.star.skill-learning: Retired into core by ADR 0377: the app's own skill review owns the skill library now, so shipping the plugin again would put a second writer on ~/.agents/skills.
//io.github.czp0312.subscription-quota: Retired 2026-11-04: this deployment does not track subscription quota.
//io.github.xinzhihong.group-rooms: Retired 2026-11-04: shared rooms are unused in this deployment.
//io.github.xideadev.pi-wechatbot: Retired 2026-11-04: the WeChat bridge is unused in this deployment.
//local.hindsight.memory: Retired 2026-11-04: this deployment does not bundle the Hindsight memory bridge.
//local.unipi: Retired 2026-11-04: the Muse learning adaptation is unused in this deployment.
//theme-plugins: Retired 2026-11-06: a declarative theme plugin costs a whole host process (~30 MB) on every launch and needs none of it. Built-in color schemes cover appearance; see ADR 0412.
//theme-plugins-extra: Retired 2026-11-06: same host-process cost as //theme-plugins. Theme authoring belongs in the app; skins ship as data, not as plugins.
//native-helper-terminals: Retired 2026-11-06: both terminals launch an unsigned helper binary (fancy-pty-helper.exe / pi-conpty-helper.exe) from the app's own resource directory. On a host with behaviour-based endpoint protection, an unsigned app spawning unknown executables it shipped itself is indistinguishable from a dropper and gets the whole app flagged. local.terminal covers the same feature in pure JavaScript.
//pi.clipboard-history: Retired 2026-11-17: the plugin's own capture service polls the host history every 2 s and mirrors it into a plaintext archive that is kept for 30 days, so the app spends its whole run reading clipboard content and writing it to disk - the exact shape behaviour-based endpoint protection calls a clipboard stealer, and this deployment's KES quarantined the app's binaries under PDM:Trojan.Win32.Generic while it was running. The host API stays: pi.clipboard.getHistory() records explicit writes and Composer pastes only, with no background sampling, which is the surface the app itself needs. Hermes parity: clipboard is read on an explicit request, never polled.
//cn.star.computer-use: Retired 2026-11-17 with packages/computer-use: a desktop-automation surface that injects input, runs in a hidden context and mirrors the screen is indistinguishable from a remote-access tool to a behaviour engine, and it was quarantined as such in this deployment. Bundling it also required the native capture package and its own driver, so the plugin, the package and the release copy were all removed together.
//development-harness-only: Retired 2026-11-06: development fixtures. One is an offline-harness manifest, the other an API probe; neither is a user-facing feature.
//duplicate-usage-views: Retired 2026-11-06: io.github.new-beginner.session-usage is the tracked pick and covers the same accounting; shipping three more usage panels only adds host processes.
//community.workbuddy-connect: Retired 2026-11-14: WorkBuddy is a built-in provider now (ADR 0397). The app starts the very same bridge out of apps/desktop/resources/in-app-providers and registers the provider row itself, so the plugin is a second gateway for one account - it cannot bind the loopback port the app owns, and a user who still has it enabled gets a provider row pointing at a key that is not theirs. The plugin's dashboard and its credential directory (~/.pi-workbuddy-connect) stay in use by the in-app gateway.
//duplicate-browser: Retired 2026-11-06: pi.browser is the tracked browser plugin; a second browser plugin doubles the CDP surface for no extra capability.
//market-translator: Retired 2026-11-06: the marketplace feed is not reachable from this deployment, so a catalog translator has nothing to translate.
//billion-context: Retired 2026-11-24: the function is already in the kernel, and the plugin's implementation is the shape this deployment gets flagged for. crates/agent-core/src/aging.rs ages old tool results inside the request (tool output measured at 94.6% of a 40-turn transcript's tokens) once the window is under pressure, and crates/agent-core/src/compaction.rs asks the model for a checkpoint summary with a retained-tail fallback, chunking and a re-anchor directive - the same class of capability, with no extra process. The plugin added an out-of-process compressor instead: a detached node proxy daemon, a loopback listener, global fetch/WebSocket interception and request-body rewriting. That daemon is what the endpoint agent reported on this machine - 9 x 4662 events with Confidence 00000006 on 2026-11-24, one of them escalating into the PDM verdict that quarantined the app. Lost capability: the upstream SQLite-backed folding store and its per-range bookkeeping, which survived restarts independently of the transcript. Nothing is lost from the conversation itself - the kernel keeps every message and re-derives the request on each send.
//local.pi-markdown: Retired 2026-11-24: the transcript already renders markdown and owns its own prose/code-block styling, so this was an 18.2 MB second copy of a renderer responsibility - the single largest item in the bundle, for a surface nothing in the product links to. Lost: its markdown file view and the pi-markdown.open command.
//local.diff-view: Retired 2026-11-24: the review panel in the core shows the same working-tree diff; this plugin contributed a view, a command and an agentExtensions hook for that same surface. Lost: the standalone diff view and its diff-view.open command.
//io.github.liushunqiu.pi-idea-git: Retired 2026-11-24: two views and two commands that shell out to an IDE for git actions, duplicating the host's open-in-editor action with their own spawn path. Lost: the in-IDE git shortcuts.
//cc.mcii.session-notify: Retired 2026-11-24: notification delivery belongs to the host, which already raises session events; this plugin registered a service and a command for it. Its foreground-window probe had already been reduced to answering "unknown" on Windows, because the hidden inline-C# probe it replaced was itself a scored shape. Lost: the opt-in notify command.
//io.github.eureka-0x01.open-with: Retired 2026-11-24: one host API (shell.openPath) behind a plugin with a single permission, called by nothing in the product. Lost: the open-with command.
//io.github.w1ndys.pi-open-in-vscode: Retired 2026-11-24: a one-command wrapper around opening a path in VS Code, already covered by the host's open-in-editor action. Lost: that command.
//io.github.w1ndys.pi-open-git-web: Retired 2026-11-24: a one-command wrapper that opens the repository host's web page, already covered by shell.openExternal. Lost: that command.
//local.terminal: Retired 2026-11-24: the last shipped carrier of the shape the kernel work removed. spawn("python3", ["-c", RELAY_SRC, cwd, cols, rows]) puts an entire Python program on a command line - the inline-interpreter-payload pattern - to build a PTY relay. It is also macOS-only in practice: the relay imports pty, termios, fcntl and pwd, spawns with a /usr/bin:/bin PATH, the IME helper returns unsupported outside darwin, and the package has no win32/conpty branch at all, so on Windows the panel cannot work even when enabled (it was already default-disabled there). Lost: the embedded xterm.js terminal panel on the platforms where it worked.
//local.pi-bot: Retired 2026-11-24: 7.67 MB, the second-largest bundled plugin and the only one still able to touch a capture device. renderer/speech-capture.mjs calls getUserMedia and is imported by voice.mjs, microphone-panel.mjs and attachment-upload.mjs, so opening the voice view asks for the microphone; the backend also starts powershell -File for DPAPI/OCR and opens loopback listeners for its MCP bridges. Its hidden microphone recorder had already been deleted at packaging time and the plugin shipped switched off on Windows - retiring it removes the capability instead of hiding it. Lost: the bot's browser-extension integration, voice input and its MCP bridges.
//com.vastsa.side-chat: Retired 2026-11-25: the deployment asked for it out of the bundle. A second chat surface that reads the current session's transcript and posts a reply back into it costs a host plugin for a conversation the main transcript already covers. Lost: the docked side chat view and its reply-into-session action.
//io.github.muzimu217.session-import: Retired 2026-11-25: the deployment asked for it out of the bundle, named for its second view (会话熔炉 / Session Forge). One plugin carried both surfaces, so retiring the plugin retires the importer with it. Lost: importing sessions from ZCode, WorkBuddy, Claude Code, Codex, OpenCode and Pi; the declarative JSON custom-source extension; the forge's distillation of those sessions into project conventions and reusable practices; both commands and their settings pages. Its session.import / project.create / agent.complete surfaces go with it.
//adoin.panel.anywhere: Retired 2026-11-25: the deployment asked for it out of the bundle — this is the plugin the plugin page lists as "Agents Anywhere 远程连接". It holds a standing outbound WebSocket from the app to api.agents-anywhere.com / web.agents-anywhere.com and gives that server the workspace chat, the session list and the approval prompts, so a deployment that does not use the service keeps a remote-control surface open for nothing. Lost: the connection-settings panel, its connector, its per-project profiles and the remote approval channel.
//pi.agents-anywhere: Retired 2026-11-25: the deployment asked for it out of the bundle — this is the earlier carrier of the same bridge, listed as "Agents Anywhere 远程助手". Keeping it would re-open the outbound socket the panel above gives up, from a second process with its own sandbox. Lost: phone/web remote viewing of a Pi session, remote questions and remote approval.
